article_title: Integration in the Achievement Motivation Literature and the Hierarchical Model of Achievement Motivation
citation: Andrew J. Elliot · Nicolas Sommet. (2023). Integration in the Achievement Motivation Literature and the Hierarchical Model of Achievement Motivation. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-023-09785-7
title: 2 × 2 standards model of achievement goals: definition and valence components
description: Within the hierarchical model, achievement goals are conceptualized in the 2 × 2 standards model in terms of two components of competence: definition (task-/self-based mastery vs. other-based performance standard) and valence (approach of success vs. avoidance of failure). Crossing these yields four goals: mastery-approach, mastery-avoidance, performance-approach, and performance-avoidance. An achievement goal is defined as 'a cognitive representation of a future competence-based possibility that a person is committed to approach or avoid.'
requirements: Goals are viewed as the conceptual centerpiece or hub of the hierarchical model, emerging from and serving underlying energization
constraints: Achievement goals alone are not sufficient to account for competence-motivated behavior; the energization source must also be identified
target_learning_goals: competence strivings and achievement goal adoption
examples: Example goals as printed: 'I am trying to do better than I have done before' (mastery-approach) and 'I am trying to avoid doing poorly compared to others' (performance-avoidance)
